newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann sees rise in 96/97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann sees rise in 96/97 profit.

text.p: German publishing group Bertelsmann AG said it expects moderate sales growth of around one billion marks and a slight rise in profit in the 1996/97 fiscal year,
"The board expects moderate sales growth of around one billion marks and a slight rise in profit in 1996/97," the company said.

The company said earlier its 1995/96 net profit rose to 905 million marks ($600.9 million) from 817 million marks, though operating profit declined to 1.53 billion marks from 1.665 billion marks. Group sales rose to 21.538 billion marks from 20.554 billion marks.

Chief financial officer Siegfried Luther told reporters, "The good profit in 1995/96 is partially attributable to special factors, which more than compensated for a slight decline in operating profit."
Gruner + Jahr, Germany's largest magazine publisher, accounted for one-third of Bertelsmann's total operating profit.

The entertainment division, which included record companies and television activities, accounted for 20 percent of operating profit. For the first time it made the second largest contribution to group profit, outpacing the printing operations of the industry division, which accounted for 15 percent of operating profit.

Sales grew 3.6 percent in Germany and were up 1.3 percent in the rest of Europe, while turnover rose 6.2 percent in the U.S. There was a 21.5 percent rise in sales in other parts of the world, largely attributable to improved music business in Japan. ($ = 1.506 German Marks)
